dictionary.definition: the set of electrical processes in heart cells that generate and propagate excitation of the heart muscle.
a sequence of heart contractions characterized by their frequency and regularity.
an atom or group of atoms with a positive or negative electric charge due to the loss or gain of electrons.
a quantity indicating the potential energy of an electric charge at a given point per unit of charge.
the difference in electric potentials between two points, which is called voltage and is measured in volts.

connection_explanations.Input impedance: input impedance affects how closely the measured potential difference corresponds to the potential difference that existed before the instrument was connected.
connection_explanations.Differential measurement: Electric potential difference is the quantity we want to determine between two points. Differential measurement is a method of determining it in which the device directly measures the voltage difference between two inputs. Differential measurement makes it possible to determine the electric potential difference between two points. In our electrocardiograph, it is the change in this difference between the selected electrodes that is used to obtain the ECG signal.

dictionary.definition: the process by which a change in electrical state propagates sequentially from one group of heart muscle cells to another.
a method of recording the electrical activity of the heart by measuring the change in potential difference between specific points on the body.
a conductive element that provides electrical contact between the body surface and a measuring device.
the time required to complete one cycle of a repeating process; for example, at 60 heart contractions per minute, one cycle lasts approximately one second.

connection_explanations.Sampling rate: The sampling rate determines the time interval between successive signal measurements. At a rate of 500 Hz, this interval is 1/500 of a second, or 2 milliseconds. It should not be confused with the repetition period of cardiac cycles.
connection_explanations.R–R interval: the R–R interval indicates the time between successive occurrences of a characteristic electrical event in the cardiac cycle. When the intervals have a constant duration, it corresponds to the repetition period of these events.

dictionary.definition: the number of measurements of a continuous signal taken in one second. Measured in hertz (Hz).

connection_explanations.Period: The sampling rate determines the time interval between successive signal measurements. At a rate of 500 Hz, this interval is 1/500 of a second, or 2 milliseconds. It should not be confused with the repetition period of cardiac cycles.

dictionary.definition: determining the voltage difference between two inputs instead of measuring each voltage relative to a common conductor.

Differential measurement is a method of determining it in which the device directly measures the voltage difference between two inputs. Differential measurement makes it possible to determine the electric potential difference between two points. dictionary.definition: a small programmable computer whose main components are combined in a single integrated circuit. It contains a processor, memory, and means of interacting with other electronic devices.
dictionary.connections: SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface), Analog-to-digital converter (ADC), Development board, Firmware, Register, Printed circuit board, Data buffer, Galvanic isolation, API (Application Programming Interface), Voltage regulator, Digital filter

connection_explanations.SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface): the microcontroller uses SPI to send commands to the measurement integrated circuit and receive the results of its operation.
connection_explanations.Analog-to-digital converter (ADC): the ADC converts the measured voltage into a number, and the microcontroller receives this number and performs the actions specified by the program.
connection_explanations.Development board: the microcontroller executes the program, while the development board provides the conditions for its operation and interaction with other components.
connection_explanations.Firmware: the microcontroller is a device that executes commands, while the firmware determines the sequence of these commands. Changing the firmware allows the behavior of the microcontroller to be changed without changing its electronic circuit.
connection_explanations.Register: the microcontroller executes a program that reads and changes the contents of the ADS1291 registers via SPI. This enables the program to control the operation of the measurement integrated circuit.
connection_explanations.Printed circuit board: the ESP32-S3 microcontroller is already installed on a ready-made development board. We are creating a separate board for the ADS1291 so that it can be connected to the microcontroller and provided with the necessary operating conditions.
connection_explanations.Data buffer: the microcontroller places the values received from the ADS1291 in a buffer so that delays in transmission to the computer do not interfere with the timely reception of new measurements.
connection_explanations.Galvanic isolation: the microcontroller can exchange digital data with a device on the other side of an isolation barrier through an interface specifically designed for this purpose.
connection_explanations.API (Application Programming Interface): the program running on the ESP32-S3 microcontroller can access the server's API via Wi-Fi. In this case, the microcontroller transmits data, while the API defines how the receiving system should process the request.
connection_explanations.Voltage regulator: the voltage regulator provides the electrical conditions necessary for the microcontroller to operate. The microcontroller itself executes the program, while the voltage regulator maintains its power supply.
connection_explanations.Digital filter: the microcontroller's program can perform digital filter calculations. In our project, this processing can initially also be performed on the computer after the data is received.

dictionary.definition: an electronic device that converts a continuously varying electrical voltage into a sequence of numbers. To do this, it measures the voltage at specific time intervals and assigns a digital value to each result.
dictionary.connections: Microcontroller, SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface), Digital filter

connection_explanations.Microcontroller: the ADC converts the measured voltage into a number, and the microcontroller receives this number and performs the actions specified by the program.
connection_explanations.SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface): the ADC converts electrical voltage into a number, while SPI allows this number to be transmitted to the microcontroller.
connection_explanations.Digital filter: the ADC converts electrical voltage into a sequence of numbers, while the digital filter processes this sequence to reduce the influence of interference.

dictionary.definition: a method of serial digital data exchange between electronic devices. The transmission of individual bits is synchronized by clock pulses.

connection_explanations.Microcontroller: the microcontroller uses SPI to send commands to the measurement integrated circuit and receive the results of its operation.
connection_explanations.Analog-to-digital converter (ADC): the ADC converts electrical voltage into a number, while SPI allows this number to be transmitted to the microcontroller.
